parole.testo: Borrowed from English to fire, eventually from Proto-Germanic *fōr. Said in several sources to be the only loan verb from English that is morphologically fully integrated.

Italianized form of English kettle, from Proto-Germanic *katilaz. Borrowed in the 19th century when the Maltese were yet little acquainted with the English language, hence treated phonetically and morphologically like a native word, compare pufta, bajla and nippla.

parole.significato: to miss (long for someone or something that is far or absent)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English to miss, from Proto-Germanic *missijaną. Superseded spelling of mmissja.
